'''Francisco''' "'''Kiko'''" '''Casilla Cortés''' ({{IPA|es|ˈkiko kaˈsiʎa}}; born 2 October 1986) is a Spanish former professional [[association football|footballer]] who played as a [[goalkeeper (association football)|goalkeeper]].

He started playing for [[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid]], but only represented the [[reserve team]]s in the early stage of his career. He went on to appear in 126 competitive matches for [[RCD Espanyol|Espanyol]] over six [[La Liga]] seasons before returning to his previous club in 2015, with whom he won three [[UEFA Champions League]] titles as backup to [[Keylor Navas]]. In [[2019–20 EFL Championship|2019–20]], he won promotion to the [[Premier League]] with [[Leeds United F.C.|Leeds United]].

Casilla won one [[cap (sport)|cap]] for [[Spain national football team|Spain]], in 2014.

==Club career==
===Real Madrid===
Born in [[Alcover]], [[Province of Tarragona|Tarragona]], [[Catalonia]], Casilla did not enjoy much playing time in his two-year stint with [[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid]] reserve side, [[Real Madrid Castilla]]. In the [[2005–06 Segunda División|2005–06 season]], he played in [[Segunda División]] after having graduated from the [[Real Madrid C|C team]], being only third choice after [[Jordi Codina]] and [[David Cobeño]].<ref name=VAVEL>{{cite web|url=https://www.vavel.com/es/futbol/2017/10/02/real-madrid/833674-felicidades-kiko.html|title=¡Felicidades, Kiko!|trans-title=Happy birthday, Kiko!|publisher=Vavel|first=Christian|last=Lancho|language=es|date=2 October 2017|access-date=17 January 2019}}</ref>

After only four appearances, Casilla was expected to receive more opportunities after the departure of Cobeño. However, Codina became the starter and [[Antonio Adán]], a fellow youth graduate, the backup, and Casilla ended up playing only in the last game of [[2006–07 Segunda División|the campaign]], with an eventual relegation befalling.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.vavel.com/es/futbol/2013/11/26/real-madrid/305872.html|title=La última plantilla que descendió con el Castilla. ¿Qué fue de ellos?|trans-title=The last squad to be relegated with Castilla. What happened to them?|publisher=Vavel|first=Miguel Ángel|last=Balderas|language=es|date=26 November 2013|access-date=20 January 2020}}</ref><ref name=VAVEL/>

===Espanyol===
[[File:Kiko Casilla.png|thumb|left|170px|Casilla in 2013]]
In August 2007, Casilla was acquired by [[RCD Espanyol|Espanyol]] on a [[free transfer (association football)|free transfer]]. On 20 January 2008, he made his debut in [[La Liga]] in a 2–1 away loss against [[Real Valladolid]], coming on as a [[Substitute (association football)|substitute]] for injured [[Iñaki Lafuente]] two minutes after [[half-time]] as the habitual starter [[Carlos Kameni]] was away on [[2008 Africa Cup of Nations|international duty]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.marca.com/marcador/futbol/2007_08/primera/jornada_20/vad_esp/|title=Llorente tumba al Espanyol|trans-title=Llorente downs Espanyol|newspaper=[[Marca (newspaper)|Marca]]|first=Almudena|last=Rivera|language=es|date=20 January 2008|access-date=1 April 2014}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=http://archivo.marca.com/edicion/marca/futbol/1a_division/espanyol/es/desarrollo/1080468.html|title=La ausencia de Kameni y la lesión de Lafuente hacen debutar a Casilla|trans-title=Kameni's absence and Lafuente's injury enable Casilla's debut|newspaper=Marca|language=es|date=21 January 2008|access-date=6 May 2016}}</ref> That month, news surfaced that [[Arsenal F.C.|Arsenal]] were interested in acquiring the young Spaniard's services.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.tribalfootball.com/article.php?id=71963|title=Arsenal interested in youngster|publisher=Tribal Football|date=2 January 2008|access-date=2 January 2008|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080105051512/http://www.tribalfootball.com/article.php?id=71963|archive-date=5 January 2008}}</ref>

Barred by Kameni and new signing [[Cristian Álvarez (footballer, born 1985)|Cristian Álvarez]], Casilla joined [[Segunda División B]] side [[Cádiz CF|Cádiz]] on loan for [[2008–09 Segunda División B|2008–09]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.mundodeportivo.com/20080726/kiko-casilla-al-cadiz-fredson-al-goias_53507541286.html|title=Kiko Casilla, al Cádiz; Fredson, al Goias|trans-title=Casilla, to Cádiz; Fredson, to Goiás|newspaper=[[Mundo Deportivo]]|language=es|date=26 July 2008|access-date=14 January 2019}}</ref> The move was extended for the entirety of the following campaign after the [[Andalusia]]ns returned to division two, and he again started most of [[2009–10 Segunda División|the season]], but the team was immediately relegated.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.lavozdigital.es/deportes/cadizcf/noticias/cadiz-cf/como-recibira-carranza-a-kiko-casilla.html|title=¿Cómo recibirá Carranza a Kiko Casilla?|trans-title=How will the Carranza welcome Kiko Casilla?|publisher=La Voz Digital|first=Alfonso|last=Carbonell|language=es|date=2 December 2015|access-date=14 January 2019}}</ref>

Casilla still sat on the bench for Espanyol's first game in [[2010–11 La Liga|2010–11]] but, on 31 August 2010, moved again on loan to second division club [[FC Cartagena|Cartagena]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.marca.com/2010/09/01/futbol/equipos/cartagena/1283296082.html|title=Casilla jugará en el Cartagena una temporada|trans-title=Casilla will play with Cartagena one season|newspaper=Marca|language=es|date=1 September 2010|access-date=5 June 2013}}</ref> Subsequently returned to the ''Pericos'', he constantly battled for first-choice status with Álvarez.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.marca.com/2012/07/24/futbol/equipos/espanyol/1343135054.html|title=Casilla: "La competencia con Cristian Álvarez es bonita"|trans-title=Casilla: "The competition with Cristian Álvarez is a beautiful thing"|newspaper=Marca|language=es|date=24 July 2012|access-date=5 June 2013}}</ref>

After the Argentine left, Casilla became the undisputed starter. On 1 February 2015, he was [[Ejection (sports)|sent off]] against [[Sevilla FC|Sevilla]] for handling [[Iago Aspas]]' shot outside of the penalty area, and his replacement [[Pau López]] could not prevent an eventual 2–3 defeat.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.foxsports.com/soccer/story/sevilla-3-espanyol-2-iago-aspas-winner-short-handed-espanyol-la-liga-sunday-scores-020115|title=Iago Aspas' late winner gives Sevilla vengeful win against Espanyol|publisher=[[Fox Sports]]|date=1 February 2015|access-date=1 February 2015}}</ref>

===Return to Real Madrid===
On 17 July 2015, Casilla returned to Real Madrid on a five-year contract for €6 million.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2015/07/official-announcement-kiko-casilla|title=Official announcement: Kiko Casilla|publisher=Real Madrid CF|date=17 July 2015|access-date=17 July 2015}}</ref> He made his competitive debut on 31 October, in a 3–1 win over [[UD Las Palmas|Las Palmas]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.laliga.es/noticias/el-real-madrid-se-aferra-al-liderato-y-sigue-invicto|title=El Real Madrid se aferra al liderato y sigue invicto|trans-title=Real Madrid cling on to first place and are still undefeated|publisher=[[La Liga]]|language=es|date=31 October 2015|access-date=31 October 2015}}</ref>

Casilla played understudy to [[Keylor Navas]] in his [[2015–16 La Liga|first season]],<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.marca.com/2015/12/04/futbol/equipos/real_madrid/1449219675.html|title='Sanción' para Kiko Casilla|trans-title=‘Sanction’ for Kiko Casilla|newspaper=Marca|first=David|last=G. Medina|language=es|date=4 December 2015|access-date=8 January 2019}}</ref> appearing in seven official matches. Two of those came in the [[2015–16 UEFA Champions League|group stage]] of the [[UEFA Champions League]],<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/news/0253-0d808b5dee55-c14b9369e018-1000--ronaldo-inspired-madrid-hold-off-shakhtar/|title=Ronaldo-inspired Madrid hold off Shakhtar|publisher=UEFA|date=25 November 2015|access-date=29 April 2025}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/news/0228-0e92cb1b045d-13a834dc2ded-1000--ronaldo-rampant-as-madrid-put-eight-past-malmo/|title=Ronaldo rampant as Madrid put eight past Malmö|publisher=UEFA|first=Joseph|last=Walker|date=8 December 2015|access-date=30 May 2016}}</ref> as the tournament ended in conquest.<ref name=CL>{{cite web|url=https://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/news/022d-0e957c5979eb-37493cb53cd0-1000--spot-on-real-madrid-defeat-atletico-in-final-again/|title=Spot-on Real Madrid defeat Atlético in final again|publisher=UEFA|first=Andrew|last=Haslam|date=28 May 2016|access-date=29 May 2016}}</ref>

On 9 August 2016, Casilla was in goal for injured Navas in the [[2016 UEFA Super Cup|3–2 victory]] against fellow Spaniards Sevilla in the [[UEFA Super Cup]], in [[Trondheim]].<ref name=SC>{{cite web|url=http://www.espnfc.co.uk/report?gameId=450351|title=Dani Carvajal's late goal in ET helps Real Madrid win UEFA Super Cup|publisher=[[ESPN FC]]|date=9 August 2016|access-date=9 August 2016}}</ref> He managed to contribute more in his [[2016–17 La Liga|second year]],<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.goal.com/es/news/4193/an%C3%A1lisis/2017/04/01/34219182/kiko-casilla-titular-por-16%C2%AA-vez-con-estad%C3%ADsticas-similares|title=Kiko Casilla – Titular por 16ª vez con estadísticas similares a las de Keylor Navas|trans-title=Kiko Casilla – Starter for the 16th time with similar statistics to those of Keylor Navas|publisher=[[Goal (website)|Goal]]|first=Alberto|last=Piñero|language=es|date=1 April 2017|access-date=22 May 2017}}</ref> and the club won the national championship after a five-year wait.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.laliga.es/noticias/real-madrid-campeon-de-laliga-santander-2016-17|title=El Real Madrid, campeón de LaLiga Santander 2016/17|trans-title=Real Madrid, LaLiga Santander champions 2016/17|publisher=La Liga|language=es|date=21 May 2017|access-date=22 May 2017}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/39926301|title=Malaga 0–2 Real Madrid|publisher=[[BBC Sport]]|date=21 May 2017|access-date=22 May 2017}}</ref> His [[2016–17 UEFA Champions League|Champions League]] input consisted of the 2–1 group phase defeat of [[Sporting CP]],<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.rtp.pt/noticias/liga-dos-campeoes/real-madrid-2-1-sporting_e947220|title=Real Madrid 2–1 Sporting|publisher=[[Rádio e Televisão de Portugal]]|language=pt|date=14 September 2016|access-date=6 June 2017}}</ref> as they again emerged victorious in the competition.<ref name=CL2>{{cite web|url=https://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/news/0250-0c5117c008df-de0901ea6dae-1000--majestic-real-madrid-win-champions-league-in-cardiff/|title=Majestic Real Madrid win Champions League in Cardiff|publisher=UEFA|first=Andrew|last=Haslam|date=3 June 2017|access-date=4 June 2017}}</ref>

Casilla made two appearances in the [[2017–18 UEFA Champions League|Champions League]]<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.rcnradio.com/deportes/asi-llegan-las-plantillas-de-real-madrid-y-liverpool-la-final-de-la-champions|title=Así llegan Real Madrid y Liverpool a la final de la Champions|trans-title=That is how Real Madrid and Liverpool arrive to the Champions final|publisher=[[RCN Radio]]|language=es|date=25 May 2018|access-date=29 May 2018}}</ref> and 17 in all competitions<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.elespanol.com/elbernabeu/futbol/20180826/casilla-rechazo-auxerre-quedarse-espana/333217176_0.html|title=Casilla rechazó al Auxerre para quedarse en España|trans-title=Casilla rejected Auxerre to stay in Spain|newspaper=[[El Español]]|first=Ángela|last=Castañeda|language=es|date=26 August 2018|access-date=17 January 2019}}</ref> during [[2017–18 Real Madrid CF season|2017–18]], as Madrid won their third consecutive and 13th overall title in the tournament.<ref name=CL3>{{cite web|url=https://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/news/0245-0e98d7318379-716954065574-1000--madrid-beat-liverpool-to-complete-hat-trick/|title=Madrid beat Liverpool to complete hat-trick|publisher=UEFA|date=26 May 2018|access-date=28 May 2018}}</ref> In the [[2018–19 La Liga|following campaign]], after the summer signing of [[Chelsea F.C.|Chelsea]]'s [[Thibaut Courtois]], he was further demoted down the pecking order.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.marca.com/en/football/real-madrid/2018/08/30/5b87e14f22601d11458b465c.html|title=Zidane returns to Castilla while Casilla remains as third choice|newspaper=Marca|first1=Patricia|last1=Terroba|first2=Conor|last2=Clancy|date=30 August 2018|access-date=8 January 2019}}</ref>

===Leeds United===
On 17 January 2019, the 32-year-old Casilla moved abroad for the first time in his career and signed a four-and-a-half-year contract at [[Leeds United F.C.|Leeds United]] of the English [[EFL Championship|Championship]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.leedsunited.com/news/team-news/24407/leeds-united-sign-kiko-casilla|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190119174418/https://www.leedsunited.com/news/team-news/24407/leeds-united-sign-kiko-casilla|url-status=dead|archive-date=19 January 2019|title=Leeds United sign Kiko Casilla|publisher=Leeds United F.C.|date=17 January 2019|access-date=17 January 2019}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2019/01/official-announcement-casilla|title=Official announcement: Casilla|publisher=Real Madrid CF|date=17 January 2019|access-date=17 January 2019}}</ref> He made his debut nine days later, in a 2–1 win against [[Rotherham United F.C.|Rotherham United]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.yorkshireeveningpost.co.uk/sport/football/leeds-united/rotherham-united-1-leeds-united-2-talking-points-mateusz-klich-is-scoring-goals-kiko-casilla-stars-as-whites-left-concerned-over-pablo-hernandez-1-9559837|title=Rotherham United 1 Leeds United 2 – talking points: Mateusz Klich is scoring goals, Kiko Casilla stars as Whites left concerned over Pablo Hernandez|newspaper=[[Yorkshire Evening Post]]|first=Phil|last=Hay|date=27 January 2019|access-date=27 January 2019}}</ref>

In September 2019, Casilla was accused of [[Racism in association football|racially abusing]] [[Charlton Athletic F.C.|Charlton Athletic]] forward [[Jonathan Leko]] in a match between the two teams.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/49895031|title=Charlton v Leeds: Football Association investigates claim of racial discrimination|publisher=BBC Sport|date=1 October 2019|access-date=2 October 2019}}</ref> He was charged by [[The Football Association]] but remained available for selection during the investigation.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.leedsunited.com/en/news/club-statement-kiko-casilla|title=Club statement: Kiko Casilla|publisher=Leeds United F.C.|date=4 November 2019|access-date=5 November 2019}}</ref> On 28 February 2020, he received an eight-game ban and £60,000 fine after being found guilty.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/51628153|title=Leeds goalkeeper gets eight-match ban for racism|publisher=BBC Sport|date=28 February 2020|access-date=28 February 2020}}</ref>

Casilla played his first game in the [[Premier League]] on 16 January 2021, in a 1–0 home loss to [[Brighton & Hove Albion F.C.|Brighton & Hove Albion]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/55598708|title=Leeds 0–1 Brighton: Neal Maupay's goal ends Seagulls' winless league run|publisher=BBC Sport|first=Jonathan|last=Jurejko|date=16 January 2021|access-date=16 January 2021}}</ref> He was second-choice to young Frenchman [[Illan Meslier]] over [[2020–21 Premier League|the season]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.leeds-live.co.uk/sport/leeds-united/leeds-united-meslier-record-hart-20467614|title=Leeds United goalkeeper Illan Meslier breaks Joe Hart's 13-year Premier League record|publisher=Leeds Live|first=Joe|last=Donnohue|date=26 April 2021|access-date=1 May 2021}}</ref>

On 12 July 2021, Casilla was loaned to [[Elche CF|Elche]] for the next [[2021–22 La Liga|Spanish top-division season]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.leedsunited.com/en/news/kiko-casilla-makes-elche-loan-move|title=Kiko Casilla makes Elche loan move|publisher=Leeds United F.C.|date=12 July 2021|access-date=12 July 2021}}</ref> Initially a starter, he eventually lost his place to [[Edgar Badia]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.elespanol.com/alicante/deporte/elche-cf/20211209/badia-siempre-mantenido-confianza-mismo/633437637_0.html|title=Badía: "Siempre he mantenido la confianza en mí mismo"|trans-title=Badía: "I never lost confidence in myself"|newspaper=El Español|first=Pablo|last=Verdú|language=es|date=9 December 2021|access-date=21 April 2022}}</ref>

Casilla's contract at Leeds was terminated by mutual consent on 31 July 2022.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.teamtalk.com/leeds-united/leeds-say-goodbye-to-kiko-casilla-with-brief-statement-as-decks-are-cleared-for-popular-replacement|title=Leeds say goodbye to Kiko Casilla with brief statement as decks are cleared for popular replacement|publisher=[[365 Media Group#TEAMtalk|TEAMtalk]]|first=James|last=Marshment|date=31 July 2022|access-date=31 July 2022}}</ref>

===Getafe===
On 10 August 2022, Casilla joined [[Getafe CF|Getafe]] on a one-year deal.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://getafecf.com/Noticia/tabid/137/Article/8412/Comunicado-Oficial-Kiko-Casilla.aspx|title=Comunicado oficial {{!}} Kiko Casilla|trans-title=Official announcement {{!}} Kiko Casilla|publisher=Getafe CF|language=es|date=10 August 2022|access-date=10 August 2022}}</ref>

==International career==
[[File:Kiko Casilla 2013 Catalonia.jpg|thumb|right|Casilla playing for [[Catalonia national football team|Catalonia]] in 2013]]
Casilla represented [[Spain national football team|Spain]] at [[Spain national under-21 football team|under-21 level]] once, playing 29 minutes in a 2–0 [[Exhibition game|friendly]] defeat of [[France national under-21 football team|France]] in [[Benidorm]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.elmundo.es/elmundodeporte/2008/02/06/futbol/1202252527.html|title=España impone su potencial sobre Francia|trans-title=Spain impose their potential over France|newspaper=[[El Mundo (Spain)|El Mundo]]|first=Sergio|last=Morro|language=es|date=6 February 2008|access-date=14 January 2019}}</ref> On 29 August 2014, he was called up to full side manager [[Vicente del Bosque]]'s 23-man squad for matches against [[France national football team|France]] and [[Macedonia national football team|Macedonia]] in September, as third-choice behind [[Iker Casillas]] and [[David de Gea]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.sefutbol.com/en/these-are-players-called-matches-against-france-and-macedonia|title=These are the players called up for the matches against France and Macedonia|publisher=[[Royal Spanish Football Federation]]|date=29 August 2014|access-date=29 August 2014|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140831194953/http://www.sefutbol.com/en/these-are-players-called-matches-against-france-and-macedonia|archive-date=31 August 2014}}</ref> He only made his debut, however, on 18 November, replacing the former for the last 14 minutes of a friendly with [[Germany national football team|Germany]] in [[Vigo]] and being beaten by [[Toni Kroos]] for the game's only goal.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.marca.com/eventos/marcador/futbol/2014_15/amistosos_seleccion/5/spa_ale/|title=Experimento pasado por agua|trans-title=Soggy experiment|newspaper=Marca|first=Delfín|last=Melero|language=es|date=18 November 2014|access-date=19 November 2014}}</ref>
